items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Communicating"?
items.answer: Presenting accounting information in reports to internal and external users in a form they can use.
items.markingKey: (c) Communicating: Presenting accounting information in reports to internal and external users in a form they can use.
options: Persons inside the business, such as the owners and managers, who use accounting information to run it.
Presenting classified data in a form useful to users, as in the trial balance and financial statements.
Presenting accounting information in reports to internal and external users in a form they can use.
The process of identifying, measuring, recording and communicating the required information relating to economic events of an organisation to interested users.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about accounting and its users is correct?
items.answer: Communicating information to users is a part of accounting.
items.markingKey: (a) Correct: Communicating information to users is a part of accounting.
options: Communicating information to users is a part of accounting.
Measuring means writing transactions in the journal in order of date.
Book keeping includes the analysis and interpretation of financial statements.
Creditors are internal users of accounting information.

items.stem: Explain the following internal users of accounting information: (i) Owners (ii) Chief executive and managers.
items.answer: (i) Owners: They want to know the profit earned and the safety of the capital invested. (ii) Chief executive and managers: They need information for planning, controlling and decision making.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) They want to know the profit earned and the safety of the capital invested. (ii) They need information for planning, controlling and decision making.

items.stem: Workers of Thakur Agencies use the reported profit figures while negotiating their annual bonus. Identify the user of accounting information described.
items.answer: Labour unions
items.markingKey: (a) Labour unions. Labour unions use profit figures in wage and bonus negotiations.

items.stem: The income tax department examines the profit shown by Bose Retail for the year. Identify the user of accounting information described. Justify your answer.
items.answer: Government and tax authorities. Tax authorities use accounts to assess tax liability.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Government and tax authorities; 2 marks for the justification: Tax authorities use accounts to assess tax liability.

items.stem:
Ahuja and Sons of Pune has three people who use its accounts: the owner Lakshmi, the store manager Pooja, and the State Bank of India which has given it a cash credit limit.
(i) Classify each of them as an internal or external user. (ii) State one item of information each would look for.
items.answer: (i) Owner Lakshmi: internal; store manager Pooja: internal; bank: external. (ii) Owner: net profit and return on capital; manager: sales and cost of stock for control; bank: liquidity and repaying capacity.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Owner Lakshmi: internal; store manager Pooja: internal; bank: external. (ii) Owner: net profit and return on capital; manager: sales and cost of stock for control; bank: liquidity and repaying capacity.

items.stem:
Singh and Sons of Patna has three people who use its accounts: the owner Fatima, the store manager Harleen, and the State Bank of India which has given it a cash credit limit.
(i) Classify each of them as an internal or external user. (ii) State one item of information each would look for.
items.answer: (i) Owner Fatima: internal; store manager Harleen: internal; bank: external. (ii) Owner: net profit and return on capital; manager: sales and cost of stock for control; bank: liquidity and repaying capacity.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Owner Fatima: internal; store manager Harleen: internal; bank: external. (ii) Owner: net profit and return on capital; manager: sales and cost of stock for control; bank: liquidity and repaying capacity.

items.stem:
Shreya says, "I am small. My book keeper writes every transaction in the books, so I already have accounting." Her accountant friend Manish disagrees.
(i) Is Shreya right? Explain with reference to the stages of accounting. (ii) List four things accounting would give her that book keeping alone does not. (iii) Who in her business should do each stage?
items.answer: (i) No. Book keeping covers only identifying and recording (and classifying); accounting also summarises, analyses, interprets and communicates the results. (ii) Profit or loss for the year; financial position (balance sheet); analysis of trends and ratios for decisions; reports for banks, tax authorities and other users. (iii) Book keeping by a junior book keeper; summarising, analysis and reporting by a qualified accountant.
items.markingKey: 6 marks: (i) No. Book keeping covers only identifying and recording (and classifying); accounting also summarises, analyses, interprets and communicates the results. (ii) Profit or loss for the year; financial position (balance sheet); analysis of trends and ratios for decisions; reports for banks, tax authorities and other users. (iii) Book keeping by a junior book keeper; summarising, analysis and reporting by a qualified accountant.

items.stem: Kapoor and Sons has applied to a bank for a loan of ₹25 lakh. The bank studies its accounts before deciding. Identify the user of accounting information described. Justify your answer.
items.answer: Banks and financial institutions. A lender needs to judge the ability to repay the loan with interest.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Banks and financial institutions; 2 marks for the justification: A lender needs to judge the ability to repay the loan with interest.

items.stem:
Rao Retail of Nagpur has three people who use its accounts: the owner Fatima, the store manager Farhan, and the State Bank of India which has given it a cash credit limit.
(i) Classify each of them as an internal or external user. (ii) State one item of information each would look for.
items.answer: (i) Owner Fatima: internal; store manager Farhan: internal; bank: external. (ii) Owner: net profit and return on capital; manager: sales and cost of stock for control; bank: liquidity and repaying capacity.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Owner Fatima: internal; store manager Farhan: internal; bank: external. (ii) Owner: net profit and return on capital; manager: sales and cost of stock for control; bank: liquidity and repaying capacity.

items.stem: Explain any four internal users of accounting information.
items.answer: (i) Owners: They want to know the profit earned and the safety of the capital invested. (ii) Chief executive and managers: They need information for planning, controlling and decision making. (iii) Plant and store managers: They need cost and sales information about their units. (iv) Business unit heads: They compare the performance of their units with targets.
items.markingKey: Any four points, 1½ marks each (heading and explanation): (i) Owners: They want to know the profit earned and the safety of the capital invested. (ii) Chief executive and managers: They need information for planning, controlling and decision making. (iii) Plant and store managers: They need cost and sales information about their units. (iv) Business unit heads: They compare the performance of their units with targets.

items.stem: Explain the following external users of accounting information: (i) Customers (ii) Labour unions.
items.answer: (i) Customers: They want to know whether the firm will continue to supply goods and honour warranties. (ii) Labour unions: They use profit figures in wage and bonus negotiations.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) They want to know whether the firm will continue to supply goods and honour warranties. (ii) They use profit figures in wage and bonus negotiations.

items.stem: State any three objectives of accounting.
items.answer: Maintaining records of business transactions; Calculating profit or loss; Depicting the financial position; Providing accounting information to users
items.markingKey: Any three of: Maintaining records of business transactions; Calculating profit or loss; Depicting the financial position; Providing accounting information to users (1 mark each).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about objectives and limitations of accounting is correct?
items.answer: Window dressing is a limitation of accounting.
items.markingKey: (a) Correct: Window dressing is a limitation of accounting.
options: Window dressing is a limitation of accounting.
Accounting can predict the future profit of a business accurately.
Accounting figures are never affected by estimates.
Accounting shows the current market value of every asset.

items.stem: Kavya no longer has to remember which customers owe her money, since every credit sale is in the books. Which objective or advantage of accounting is served here?
items.answer: Replaces memory
items.markingKey: (c) Replaces memory. Records remove dependence on memory.
options: Serves as evidence in legal matters

items.stem: The GST officer accepted the returns of Banerjee Enterprises because its books were properly maintained. Which objective or advantage of accounting is served here? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Helps in settlement of tax liability. Properly kept accounts are accepted by tax authorities.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Helps in settlement of tax liability; 2 marks for the justification: Properly kept accounts are accepted by tax authorities.

items.stem:
Varun owns Bose and Sons, Guwahati. A competitor shows a higher profit than Bose and Sons, but Varun knows the competitor bought its machinery 20 years ago at low prices, while Bose and Sons bought new machinery last year. The competitor also has a famous brand that does not appear in its balance sheet.
(i) Identify two limitations of accounting illustrated here. (ii) Explain why Varun should be careful while comparing the two profits.
items.answer: (i) Ignores price level changes (old machinery at historical cost gives low depreciation); ignores qualitative elements (brand value not recorded). (ii) Profits are based on historical costs and leave out non-money factors, so they are not strictly comparable.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Ignores price level changes (old machinery at historical cost gives low depreciation); ignores qualitative elements (brand value not recorded). (ii) Profits are based on historical costs and leave out non-money factors, so they are not strictly comparable.

items.stem: An investor complains that the latest accounts of Malhotra Agencies tell him what happened last year, not what will happen next year. Which limitation of accounting does this illustrate? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Historical in nature. Accounting records past transactions and does not predict the future.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Historical in nature; 2 marks for the justification: Accounting records past transactions and does not predict the future.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the limitations of accounting?
items.answer: Helps in the sale of a business
items.markingKey: (b) "Helps in the sale of a business" is one of the advantages of accounting, not one of the limitations of accounting.
options: Helps in the sale of a business

items.stem: Just before the year end, Iyer Enterprises delayed payments to suppliers so that its cash balance would look large to the bank. Which limitation of accounting does this illustrate?
items.answer: Can be manipulated (window dressing)
items.markingKey: (b) Can be manipulated (window dressing). Figures were arranged to show a better position than the real one.

items.stem: Gupta Stores bought land in Varanasi in 1995 for ₹8 lakh. Its balance sheet still shows ₹8 lakh, although the land would sell for ₹1.2 crore today. Which limitation of accounting does this illustrate? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Ignores price level changes. Assets stay at historical cost; the rise in prices is not shown.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Ignores price level changes; 2 marks for the justification: Assets stay at historical cost; the rise in prices is not shown.

items.stem: Fatima wants to sell her shop Kapoor Stores and the buyer agrees a price on the basis of its accounts. Which objective or advantage of accounting is served here? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Helps in the sale of a business. Accounts help to determine the value of a business.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Helps in the sale of a business; 2 marks for the justification: Accounts help to determine the value of a business.

items.stem: What is meant by "Timeliness"?
items.answer: Information is made available to decision makers before it loses its capacity to influence decisions.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Information is made available to decision makers before it loses its capacity to influence decisions.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about qualitative characteristics is correct?
items.answer: Comparability includes both intra-firm and inter-firm comparison.
items.markingKey: (a) Correct: Comparability includes both intra-firm and inter-firm comparison.
options: Comparability includes both intra-firm and inter-firm comparison.
Comparability is possible even if each firm follows a different method every year.
Reliability means information should be produced as fast as possible.
Understandability requires accounts to avoid all numbers.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about qualitative characteristics is NOT correct?
items.answer: Relevance means information must be verifiable by independent persons.
items.markingKey: (a) Incorrect statement: Relevance means information must be verifiable by independent persons.
options: Relevance means information must be verifiable by independent persons.
Timeliness is an aspect of relevance.
Comparability includes both intra-firm and inter-firm comparison.

items.stem: An investor compares the profit margins of Iyer Enterprises and Singh Industries, which both follow the same accounting standards. Which qualitative characteristic of accounting information is involved?
items.answer: Comparability
items.markingKey: (a) Comparability. Similar methods allow inter-firm comparison.

items.stem: Thakur and Sons adds plain-language notes explaining each major item in its balance sheet for small shareholders. Which qualitative characteristic of accounting information is involved? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Understandability. Clear presentation helps users understand the information.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Understandability; 2 marks for the justification: Clear presentation helps users understand the information.

items.stem:
The annual report of Iyer Retail, Dehradun, came out 10 months after the year end. It used a new depreciation method without saying so, and it was full of unexplained abbreviations.
(i) Identify the three qualitative characteristics that are missing. (ii) Suggest one improvement for each.
items.answer: (i) Relevance (not timely); comparability (method changed without disclosure); understandability (unexplained abbreviations). (ii) Publish within a few months; follow consistent methods and disclose changes; give clear headings and notes.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Relevance (not timely); comparability (method changed without disclosure); understandability (unexplained abbreviations). (ii) Publish within a few months; follow consistent methods and disclose changes; give clear headings and notes.

items.stem: Which qualitative characteristic is described here? "Information should be available in time and should influence the decisions of users by helping them form predictions or confirm earlier ones."
items.answer: Relevance
items.markingKey: (c) Relevance: Information should be available in time and should influence the decisions of users by helping them form predictions or confirm earlier ones.

items.stem: State one difference between intra-firm comparison and inter-firm comparison on the basis of meaning.
items.answer: intra-firm comparison: comparison of the same firm's results over different periods; inter-firm comparison: comparison of one firm's results with those of other firms
items.markingKey: 1 mark: intra-firm comparison: comparison of the same firm's results over different periods; inter-firm comparison: comparison of one firm's results with those of other firms

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Understandability"?
items.answer: Information should be presented so that users with reasonable knowledge can grasp its meaning in the same sense as the preparers.
items.markingKey: (d) Understandability: Information should be presented so that users with reasonable knowledge can grasp its meaning in the same sense as the preparers.
options: Information is made available to decision makers before it loses its capacity to influence decisions.
Information should allow users to compare the performance of the firm over time and with other firms.
Independent persons using the same methods would arrive at the same figures.
Information should be presented so that users with reasonable knowledge can grasp its meaning in the same sense as the preparers.

items.stem: Which of the following is true of intra-firm comparison but not of inter-firm comparison?
items.answer: Requirement: the same accounting methods must be followed year after year
items.markingKey: (d) intra-firm comparison: Requirement: the same accounting methods must be followed year after year. The other options describe inter-firm comparison.
options: Requirement: similar accounting methods must be followed by the firms compared
Purpose: to judge the firm's position in its industry
Meaning: comparison of one firm's results with those of other firms
Requirement: the same accounting methods must be followed year after year

items.stem:
Gauri, accountant of Thakur Industries, is under pressure from the owner to record an expected order of ₹5 lakh as sales this year so that the bank sees higher sales.
(i) Which qualitative characteristic would be violated? (ii) What should Gauri do and why?
items.answer: (i) Reliability: the figure would not be supported by evidence and would be biased. (ii) Refuse; record sales only when they take place, since users such as the bank depend on faithful, verifiable figures.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Reliability: the figure would not be supported by evidence and would be biased. (ii) Refuse; record sales only when they take place, since users such as the bank depend on faithful, verifiable figures.

items.stem: The accounts of Iyer Industries use so many technical codes that even an educated shareholder cannot make out what they mean. Which qualitative characteristic of accounting information is involved?
items.answer: Understandability
items.markingKey: (d) Understandability. Information must be presented in a form users can understand.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Expense"?
items.answer: The cost incurred by a business in the process of earning revenue.
items.markingKey: (d) Expense: The cost incurred by a business in the process of earning revenue.
options: Goods, spares and other items in hand at the end of an accounting period.
Persons or entities to whom the enterprise owes an amount for goods or services bought on credit.
An identifiable business enterprise, such as a sole proprietorship, partnership or company, treated as separate from its owner.
The cost incurred by a business in the process of earning revenue.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the current assets?
items.answer: Furniture and fixtures
items.markingKey: (b) "Furniture and fixtures" is one of the non-current (fixed) assets, not one of the current assets.

items.stem: Distinguish between trade discount and cash discount on the basis of shown in invoice, recording, purpose and time.
items.answer: (i) Shown in invoice: trade discount: deducted on the face of the invoice; cash discount: not shown in the invoice. (ii) Recording: trade discount: not recorded in the books; sale is recorded at net price; cash discount: recorded in the books as discount allowed or received. (iii) Purpose: trade discount: given to promote sales or for bulk purchase; cash discount: given to encourage prompt payment. (iv) Time: trade discount: allowed at the time of sale; cash discount: allowed at the time of payment.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Shown in invoice: trade discount: deducted on the face of the invoice; cash discount: not shown in the invoice. (ii) Recording: trade discount: not recorded in the books; sale is recorded at net price; cash discount: recorded in the books as discount allowed or received. (iii) Purpose: trade discount: given to promote sales or for bulk purchase; cash discount: given to encourage prompt payment. (iv) Time: trade discount: allowed at the time of sale; cash discount: allowed at the time of payment.

items.stem: Siddharth started Reddy Stores by putting ₹3,00,000 of his savings into it. What is this amount called in the books of the business?
items.answer: Capital
items.markingKey: (a) Capital. The amount invested by the owner is capital.

items.stem: Chopra Agencies sold goods with a list price of ₹95,000 to Malhotra Industries at 15% trade discount and 2% cash discount. Malhotra Industries paid immediately. Find (i) the amount of the invoice (ii) the cash discount (iii) the cash received.
items.markingKey: Trade discount 15% of ₹95,000 = ₹14,250, invoice ₹80,750 (1); cash discount 2% of ₹80,750 = ₹1,615 (1); cash received ₹79,135 (1). Only the cash discount is recorded in the books.

items.stem: Answer each part. In each case give a reason. (i) A cash memo issued by Das and Sons for a sale of ₹2,400 is kept in the file as proof of the sale. What is this document called? (ii) Das and Sons offers 10% off the list price of its kitchen appliances to a retailer who buys in bulk. What is this reduction called?
items.answer: (i) Voucher: Documentary evidence supporting a transaction is a voucher. (ii) Trade discount: A reduction on list price at the time of sale is trade discount.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Voucher (ii) Trade discount

items.stem: Sahil's capital was ₹6,80,000 on 1 April 2025 and ₹8,22,000 on 31 March 2026. During the year Sahil withdrew ₹30,000 and introduced fresh capital of ₹80,000. Calculate the profit for the year.
items.markingKey: Profit = Closing capital + Drawings − Additional capital − Opening capital = ₹8,22,000 + ₹30,000 − ₹80,000 − ₹6,80,000 = ₹92,000.

items.stem:
Manish started Saxena Retail in Mumbai with capital of ₹7,90,000 and a bank loan of ₹1,00,000 repayable in 4 years. At the end of the first month the business had furniture ₹60,000, stock ₹60,000, debtors ₹51,000, creditors ₹25,000 and the rest in cash. Assume no profit or loss yet.
(i) Find the cash balance. (ii) Classify each item as a current asset, non-current asset, current liability or non-current liability.
items.answer: (i) Cash ₹7,44,000 (ii) Furniture: non-current asset; stock, debtors, cash: current assets; creditors: current liability; bank loan: non-current liability; capital: owner's equity.
items.markingKey: (i) Assets = Liabilities + Capital: cash = ₹7,90,000 + ₹1,00,000 + ₹25,000 − ₹60,000 − ₹60,000 − ₹51,000 = ₹7,44,000 (2 marks). (ii) classification (2 marks).

items.stem: In the balance sheet of a trader, "Loan from bank repayable after 5 years" is classified as a …
items.answer: Non-current liability
items.markingKey: (d) Loan from bank repayable after 5 years is a non-current liability.

items.stem: In the balance sheet of a trader, "Bills payable" is classified as a …
items.answer: Current liability
items.markingKey: (d) Bills payable is a current liability.

items.stem: Zoya sold goods worth ₹40,000 on credit to Ishaan. In the books of Zoya, which term describes Ishaan? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Debtors. Ishaan owes money to the business for goods bought on credit.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Debtors; 2 marks for the justification: Ishaan owes money to the business for goods bought on credit.

items.stem: Shreya started the year with a capital of ₹3,40,000. During the year the business earned a profit of ₹1,75,000, and Shreya withdrew ₹36,000 for personal use. Find the capital at the end of the year.
items.markingKey: Closing capital = Opening capital + Profit + Additional capital − Drawings = ₹3,40,000 + ₹1,75,000 + ₹0 − ₹36,000 = ₹4,79,000.

items.stem: In the balance sheet of a trader, "Debentures" is classified as a …
items.answer: Non-current liability
items.markingKey: (a) Debentures is a non-current liability.

items.stem: State any three current assets.
items.answer: Cash in hand; Debtors; Stock of goods; Bills receivable; Prepaid expenses
items.markingKey: Any three of: Cash in hand; Debtors; Stock of goods; Bills receivable; Prepaid expenses (1 mark each).

items.stem: Rohan's business has total assets of ₹9,60,000 and total liabilities (excluding capital) of ₹3,40,000. What is the owner's capital?
items.markingKey: Capital = Assets − Liabilities = ₹9,60,000 − ₹3,40,000 = ₹6,20,000.

items.stem: Which of the following is one of the current assets?
items.answer: Stock of goods
items.markingKey: (a) "Stock of goods" is one of the current assets; the others are non-current (fixed) assets.

items.stem: State one difference between debtors and creditors on the basis of balance sheet.
items.answer: debtors: shown as a current asset; creditors: shown as a current liability
items.markingKey: 1 mark: debtors: shown as a current asset; creditors: shown as a current liability

items.stem: Verma Industries changes its method of stock valuation every year, so Mehak cannot compare this year's profit with last year's. Which qualitative characteristic of accounting information is involved? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Comparability. Frequent changes in method destroy comparability over time.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Comparability; 2 marks for the justification: Frequent changes in method destroy comparability over time.

items.stem:
Tanvi runs Iyer Traders, a medicines business in Bhopal. She keeps a diary of cash received and paid but no other record. Her bank has asked for the profit figure and a statement of assets and liabilities before renewing her loan, and a supplier wants to know if she can pay on time.
(i) Name the two external users mentioned and the information each needs. (ii) Why is her cash diary not enough? Suggest what she should do.
items.answer: (i) The bank: profit and repaying capacity; the supplier: short-term liquidity (ability to pay dues on time). (ii) A cash diary records only cash; it cannot show profit, credit transactions or financial position. She should maintain a complete double entry system and prepare financial statements.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) The bank: profit and repaying capacity; the supplier: short-term liquidity (ability to pay dues on time). (ii) A cash diary records only cash; it cannot show profit, credit transactions or financial position. She should maintain a complete double entry system and prepare financial statements.

items.stem: What is meant by "Revenue"?
items.answer: The amount a business earns by selling its products or providing services to customers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: The amount a business earns by selling its products or providing services to customers.

items.stem: Tanvi, owner of Joshi Industries, took ₹5,000 from the cash box to pay her son's school fees. What is this amount called? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Drawings. Cash withdrawn by the owner for personal use is drawings.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Drawings; 2 marks for the justification: Cash withdrawn by the owner for personal use is drawings.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the advantages of accounting?
items.answer: Ignores qualitative elements
items.markingKey: (c) "Ignores qualitative elements" is one of the limitations of accounting, not one of the advantages of accounting.
options: Helps in the sale of a business
Helps in settlement of tax liability

items.stem: Which accounting term is described here? "Persons inside the business, such as the owners and managers, who use accounting information to run it."
items.answer: Internal users
items.markingKey: (c) Internal users: Persons inside the business, such as the owners and managers, who use accounting information to run it.

items.stem: Ahuja and Sons sold goods with a list price of ₹1,36,000 to Joshi Enterprises at 5% trade discount and 5% cash discount. Joshi Enterprises paid immediately. Find (i) the amount of the invoice (ii) the cash discount (iii) the cash received.
items.markingKey: Trade discount 5% of ₹1,36,000 = ₹6,800, invoice ₹1,29,200 (1); cash discount 5% of ₹1,29,200 = ₹6,460 (1); cash received ₹1,22,740 (1). Only the cash discount is recorded in the books.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the internal users of accounting information?
items.answer: Customers
items.markingKey: (b) "Customers" is one of the external users of accounting information, not one of the internal users of accounting information.

items.stem:
Manish, accountant of Sharma Enterprises, is under pressure from the owner to record an expected order of ₹5 lakh as sales this year so that the bank sees higher sales.
(i) Which qualitative characteristic would be violated? (ii) What should Manish do and why?
items.answer: (i) Reliability: the figure would not be supported by evidence and would be biased. (ii) Refuse; record sales only when they take place, since users such as the bank depend on faithful, verifiable figures.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Reliability: the figure would not be supported by evidence and would be biased. (ii) Refuse; record sales only when they take place, since users such as the bank depend on faithful, verifiable figures.

items.stem: Saanvi started the year with a capital of ₹8,00,000. During the year the business earned a profit of ₹1,06,000, introduced additional capital of ₹95,000, and Saanvi withdrew ₹56,000 for personal use. Find the capital at the end of the year.
items.markingKey: Closing capital = Opening capital + Profit + Additional capital − Drawings = ₹8,00,000 + ₹1,06,000 + ₹95,000 − ₹56,000 = ₹9,45,000.

items.stem: Which of the following is true of book keeping but not of accounting?
items.answer: Analytical skill: little analytical skill is needed
items.markingKey: (b) book keeping: Analytical skill: little analytical skill is needed. The other options describe accounting.
options: Stage: it is the secondary stage that begins where book keeping ends
Analytical skill: little analytical skill is needed
Analytical skill: high analytical skill and judgement are needed
Objective: to ascertain results and financial position and communicate them

items.stem: Which limitation of accounting does this illustrate? In each case give a reason. (i) Just before the year end, Singh Agencies delayed payments to suppliers so that its cash balance would look large to the bank. (ii) The highly skilled and loyal sales team of Singh Agencies is its biggest strength, but it appears nowhere in the accounts.
items.answer: (i) Can be manipulated (window dressing): Figures were arranged to show a better position than the real one. (ii) Ignores qualitative elements: Things that cannot be measured in money are left out of accounts.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Can be manipulated (window dressing) (ii) Ignores qualitative elements

items.stem:
Ahuja Enterprises of Surat has three people who use its accounts: the owner Saanvi, the store manager Meera, and the State Bank of India which has given it a cash credit limit.
(i) Classify each of them as an internal or external user. (ii) State one item of information each would look for.
items.answer: (i) Owner Saanvi: internal; store manager Meera: internal; bank: external. (ii) Owner: net profit and return on capital; manager: sales and cost of stock for control; bank: liquidity and repaying capacity.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Owner Saanvi: internal; store manager Meera: internal; bank: external. (ii) Owner: net profit and return on capital; manager: sales and cost of stock for control; bank: liquidity and repaying capacity.

items.stem: Which of the following is true of trade discount but not of cash discount?
items.answer: Purpose: given to promote sales or for bulk purchase
items.markingKey: (c) trade discount: Purpose: given to promote sales or for bulk purchase. The other options describe cash discount.
options: Shown in invoice: not shown in the invoice
Purpose: given to encourage prompt payment
Purpose: given to promote sales or for bulk purchase
Recording: recorded in the books as discount allowed or received

items.stem: State one difference between debtors and creditors on the basis of balance in ledger.
items.answer: debtors: their accounts show a debit balance; creditors: their accounts show a credit balance
items.markingKey: 1 mark: debtors: their accounts show a debit balance; creditors: their accounts show a credit balance

items.stem: The accounts of Sharma Industries use so many technical codes that even an educated shareholder cannot make out what they mean. Which qualitative characteristic of accounting information is involved? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Understandability. Information must be presented in a form users can understand.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Understandability; 2 marks for the justification: Information must be presented in a form users can understand.

items.stem:
Om runs Das Traders, a organic food products business in Agra. He keeps a diary of cash received and paid but no other record. His bank has asked for the profit figure and a statement of assets and liabilities before renewing his loan, and a supplier wants to know if she can pay on time.
(i) Name the two external users mentioned and the information each needs. (ii) Why is his cash diary not enough? Suggest what he should do.
items.answer: (i) The bank: profit and repaying capacity; the supplier: short-term liquidity (ability to pay dues on time). (ii) A cash diary records only cash; it cannot show profit, credit transactions or financial position. He should maintain a complete double entry system and prepare financial statements.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) The bank: profit and repaying capacity; the supplier: short-term liquidity (ability to pay dues on time). (ii) A cash diary records only cash; it cannot show profit, credit transactions or financial position. He should maintain a complete double entry system and prepare financial statements.

items.stem: What is meant by "Business entity"?
items.answer: An identifiable business enterprise, such as a sole proprietorship, partnership or company, treated as separate from its owner.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: An identifiable business enterprise, such as a sole proprietorship, partnership or company, treated as separate from its owner.

items.stem: Gupta Agencies paid ₹18,000 as salary to its staff in the year. Which term describes this amount? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Expense. Cost incurred in earning revenue is an expense.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Expense; 2 marks for the justification: Cost incurred in earning revenue is an expense.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the advantages of accounting?
items.answer: Ignores qualitative elements
items.markingKey: (c) "Ignores qualitative elements" is one of the limitations of accounting, not one of the advantages of accounting.
options: Serves as evidence in legal matters
Helps in the sale of a business

items.stem: Which accounting term is described here? "Quantifying business transactions in a common unit of money."
items.answer: Measuring
items.markingKey: (b) Measuring: Quantifying business transactions in a common unit of money.

items.stem: Nair and Sons sold goods with a list price of ₹64,000 to Patel Industries at 5% trade discount and 5% cash discount. Patel Industries paid immediately. Find (i) the amount of the invoice (ii) the cash discount (iii) the cash received.
items.markingKey: Trade discount 5% of ₹64,000 = ₹3,200, invoice ₹60,800 (1); cash discount 5% of ₹60,800 = ₹3,040 (1); cash received ₹57,760 (1). Only the cash discount is recorded in the books.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the internal users of accounting information?
items.answer: Tax authorities
items.markingKey: (a) "Tax authorities" is one of the external users of accounting information, not one of the internal users of accounting information.

items.stem:
Harpreet, accountant of Singh Industries, is under pressure from the owner to record an expected order of ₹5 lakh as sales this year so that the bank sees higher sales.
(i) Which qualitative characteristic would be violated? (ii) What should Harpreet do and why?
items.answer: (i) Reliability: the figure would not be supported by evidence and would be biased. (ii) Refuse; record sales only when they take place, since users such as the bank depend on faithful, verifiable figures.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Reliability: the figure would not be supported by evidence and would be biased. (ii) Refuse; record sales only when they take place, since users such as the bank depend on faithful, verifiable figures.

items.stem: Ananya started the year with a capital of ₹5,20,000. During the year the business earned a profit of ₹1,86,000, introduced additional capital of ₹50,000, and Ananya withdrew ₹1,41,000 for personal use. Find the capital at the end of the year.
items.markingKey: Closing capital = Opening capital + Profit + Additional capital − Drawings = ₹5,20,000 + ₹1,86,000 + ₹50,000 − ₹1,41,000 = ₹6,15,000.

items.stem: Which of the following is true of book keeping but not of accounting?
items.answer: Stage: it is the primary (first) stage
items.markingKey: (b) book keeping: Stage: it is the primary (first) stage. The other options describe accounting.
options: Scope: it includes summarising, analysing, interpreting and communicating as well
Stage: it is the primary (first) stage
Analytical skill: high analytical skill and judgement are needed
Stage: it is the secondary stage that begins where book keeping ends

items.stem: Which limitation of accounting does this illustrate? In each case give a reason. (i) The highly skilled and loyal sales team of Singh Agencies is its biggest strength, but it appears nowhere in the accounts. (ii) Two accountants of Singh Agencies estimate the useful life of the same machine as 8 and 12 years, giving different profits.
items.answer: (i) Ignores qualitative elements: Things that cannot be measured in money are left out of accounts. (ii) Based on estimates: Depreciation depends on estimated life, so figures involve judgement.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Ignores qualitative elements (ii) Based on estimates

items.stem:
Sethi Brothers of Bhopal has three people who use its accounts: the owner Imran, the store manager Dev, and the State Bank of India which has given it a cash credit limit.
(i) Classify each of them as an internal or external user. (ii) State one item of information each would look for.
items.answer: (i) Owner Imran: internal; store manager Dev: internal; bank: external. (ii) Owner: net profit and return on capital; manager: sales and cost of stock for control; bank: liquidity and repaying capacity.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Owner Imran: internal; store manager Dev: internal; bank: external. (ii) Owner: net profit and return on capital; manager: sales and cost of stock for control; bank: liquidity and repaying capacity.

items.stem: Which of the following is true of trade discount but not of cash discount?
items.answer: Shown in invoice: deducted on the face of the invoice
items.markingKey: (d) trade discount: Shown in invoice: deducted on the face of the invoice. The other options describe cash discount.
options: Recording: recorded in the books as discount allowed or received
Shown in invoice: not shown in the invoice
Time: allowed at the time of payment
Shown in invoice: deducted on the face of the invoice
